pr_title: Improve handling of archives when installing assets
pr_body: Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81311. Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75712. So https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75712 has been a problem for quite some time now. As discussed, there are two key points: - Installing ZIPs manually is treated differently than installing assets from the AssetLib (despite handling the same ZIPs internally); - All ZIPs are expected to have a root directory in them, because that's how GitHub, etc pack their ZIPs. And https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81311 is a new finding, as far as I know. It seems some ZIP archives can skip the directory structure information and just contain record of files without intermediate folders. We fail at handling those gracefully. ----- So I set to fix these problems, and along the way I tweaks smaller details here and there. Here's a list of changes: * Implicitly create folders when parsing ZIP files to make sure we have the entire structure available regardless of the source ZIP. * Add a checkbox that allows to skip the root directory when extracting files, _if such directory exists_. * Fix formatting of the "Files failed to extract" error message that was missing a line break. * Fix some errors not being displayed at all (also remove the unnecessary dialog and use toasts instead). * Improve the status bar to better highlight the title of the asset and the status on the conflicting files (also use `TTRN` for that last message). * Rename the window to explain what it's for. * Various refactoring for code clarity and slightly better organization (this is clearly a very old file, and it leaves a lot to be desired, so I kept the changes to rather minimal). Most of it should be self explanatory. Regarding the checkbox, it tries to be smart. First of all, it's disabled if there is no single root folder in the asset archive. It only becomes available if your asset has a folder structure similar to what GitHub creates. This may backfire when your ZIP file contains, for example, only the `addons` folder — but if that becomes an issue we should be able to easily add an exception. I've decided to preserve the current dual logic, where assets installed through the AssetLib have their root folder skipped, while archives installed manually don't behave this way. However, this is no longer a hardcoded behavior. Instead, the checkbox is either checked by default or not, but can still be changed by the user. Here's everything in action (note that the image loading error is related to the broken asset and is not a part of this PR): https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/11782833/5e5add57-130a-4a06-b82e-09b4a4e2c4a8
pr_comments:
Would it be possible to modify what info the editor retries from the asset library to verify if the repo host is custom or not? I think that could potentially be a cleaner approach as then we would know for certain how it should be handled in either case. 

EDIT: This would not resolve issues with manual imports still, but it would help the checkbox be more accurate in assumptions for direct downloads.

A custom host doesn't mean the asset doesn't follow this structure. And a custom host can still be used to point to a GitHub archive.

Giving users control is, IMO, the best option.
@lyuma this was a big problem for our extensions and offers alternative for our problem of requiring the root to be project root and not directory addons root

> this was a big problem for our extensions and offers alternative for our problem of requiring the root to be project root and not directory addons root

I'm not sure this PR would solve your issue. But after this little refactor I'm quite confident I can implement the "export to this folder" feature, so archives can be exported to places other than the root.
Tested regarding https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81311, and it works now.
All concerns should be addressed, I think.

issue_context.title: Editor treats custom repository host zips differently.
issue_context.body:
I noticed that some plug-ins that have their repository host set as custom seem to have their zips treated differently.  For example, some plug-ins I have downloaded, the editor seems to ignore the base folders and just dump the contents into the project's root.  However, ones that have, say, Github listed as the repository host with a commit hash to get the zips, those unzip correctly.

In both cases, the editor seems to see the folders.  It just doesn't install correctly for some reason.  Not sure if this is intended, a bug, or what.
comments: Can you take a screenshot of the same asset with GitHub repository provider then Custom being installed in the editor (with the list of files to install being displayed)?

My asset is having this issue, it uses a nightly.link: https://nightly.link/WeaselGames/godot_luaAPI/workflows/gdextension/main/godot_luaAPI.zip
ZIP:
![zip](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7241029/230196509-59d21506-d6a5-493d-903d-f79064f001ca.png)
In Editor:
![editor](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7241029/230196562-01384cb0-3a57-4c49-85d6-2600da3d2ab3.png)

So here are two screens; one using a custom repo host zip and mine using a Github commit hash zip:
![screenie1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1097098/230198372-af63c067-0d57-499e-b8fb-30e650356c11.png)
![screenie2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1097098/230198379-38e65062-77ab-4bc9-9ef0-3d25da53e159.png)

Upon making these screens, I find that the Github commit hash zips have the first folder as the commit hash-named folder which the editor ignore then installs those contents; which is the correct behavior for these kinds of zips.

However, the custom repo host zips do not have these hash-named folders and just directly store the files needed.  The editor treats them the same way and skips the first folder and installs the contents inside.  So it seems to be treating both the same way actually, though this is not really ideal for most custom repo zips I have seen.
It may be a good idea to make this behavior known to people posting custom repo plug-ins so they can package accordingly.  Or if this is a flag the editor understands, to treat the zips differently.

To add to this, adding a container folder manually also semi breaks manual imports, as it is included in this case. Meaning two different versions of the asset would need to be maintained.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7241029/230213828-691505a3-d387-4430-8fa6-14a4f6d1c8c2.png)

@Calinou Will this be fixed on the Godot side? It seems to me to be an issue firmly on the side of the Asset Library and not asset creators. In short, the issue is that a ZIP file imported manually via Asset Library → Import is treated differently than _the exact same ZIP file_ specified in the Asset Library "Download Commit/URL" field. The asset is using the Custom repository host option. Here's an affected asset: https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1798. And here's the ZIP file it's downloading that can be manually imported: https://github.com/ashtonmeuser/godot-wasm/releases/download/v0.1.8-godot-3/godot-wasm.zip. Attached are screenshots of (1) manually imported ZIP file via Asset Library → Import, (2) [asset](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1798) imported via Asset Library GUI, (3) download field in Asset Library "My Assets". Note that the same ZIP file is used and results in different directory structures. It seems unfair and overly complicated to expect asset creators to build separate artifacts for the Asset Library GUI and for manual importing and for asset users to differentiate the two. How the exact same functionality in Godot was implemented twice with differing results I have no idea. As for solutions, you've put yourself in a sticky situation as some asset creators may be accounting for this idiosyncrasy and you can't break their assets. The simplest solution, in my mind, is to add a new field in the Asset Store settings along the lines of "Include ZIP top-level directory" that defaults to false. Godot will have to read this setting and extract the asset accordingly.

> It seems to me to be an issue firmly on the side of the Asset Library and not asset creators.

This means it's an issue with the editor code handling the ZIPs, not the asset library backend (which doesn't host any ZIP archives, let alone manipulate them).

This is caused by the editor being overly eager with trimming the top-level folder as said here:

> However, the custom repo host zips do not have these hash-named folders and just directly store the files needed. The editor treats them the same way and skips the first folder and installs the contents inside. So it seems to be treating both the same way actually, though this is not really ideal for most custom repo zips I have seen.

I don't see a way to fix this without breaking compatibility, but we could make it so this change applies in a new minor version (as you can't see assets from older/newer minor versions in the asset library UI). I would prefer not adding a legacy handling field to the asset library structure.

Yeah, there would be no way to fix this in the current or previous versions of Godot.  When I was originally looking at this, I thought if there was a way to pass whether it was a commit zip or not (maybe true/false), then the editor could change how it unzips things.  But, again, this wouldn't fix anything prior to said change; it is a "growing pains" kind of change.

In the interim, the easiest way to avoid this is having people submitting zips not from Github commits to add a new top-level folders that gets ignored.  Not ideal but is the fastest solution.

Agreed that the root cause of this is not the Asset Library but rather the editor.

> In the interim, the easiest way to avoid this is having people submitting zips not from Github commits to add a new top-level folders that gets ignored.

This breaks manually importing a zip file. The problem with this issue is that the trivial fix for the Asset Library ZIP breaks that same ZIP for manual imports. The inconsistency in editor treatment of assets is the issue.

Perhaps the simplest solution is for the editor to do the same trimming of top-level directory for manually imported asset ZIPs. Then the solution is, as Gramps mentioned, adding a vestigial dir to the top of the ZIP that will be ignored. This means that editors prior to the fix will work with the Asset Library but not with manual imports which is the least impactful in my opinion.

> Perhaps the simplest solution is for the editor to do the same trimming of top-level directory for manually imported asset ZIPs. Then the solution is, as Gramps mentioned, adding a vestigial dir to the top of the ZIP that will be ignored. This means that editors prior to the fix will work with the Asset Library but not with manual imports which is the least impactful in my opinion.

~~The issue is that would break downloading the repo as a zip and importing for people not using custom download links.~~
Edit: actually I am mistaken, it wouldn't

The difference in treatment of ZIP assets seems intentional and was added by @reduz in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/8b1dcbfe4d92f9d7273bbd2f1eb805e5c508961a. Opening an Asset Library archive ([addon_editor_plugin.cpp#L392](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b1dcbfe4d92f9d7273bbd2f1eb805e5c508961a/tools/editor/addon_editor_plugin.cpp#L392)) uses a depth of `1` while opening a manually downloaded archive ([addon_editor_plugin.cpp#L1032](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8b1dcbfe4d92f9d7273bbd2f1eb805e5c508961a/tools/editor/addon_editor_plugin.cpp#L1032)) uses the default depth of `0`.

The solution without a change to Godot is to package the Asset Library archive with an extra top-level directory. The caveat is that users can not download _asset_library.zip_ (or whatever you've named it) from the releases page and install it manually. They can, however, download the repo ZIP and install that manually (thus, a `.gitattributes` file is a good idea).

Edit: Speculating a little, the top-level directory that includes the hash seems like a cacheing mechanism to avoid downloading the repo multiple times.

I've opened a PR that attempts to address this situation in a simple but graceful way: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81358

Let me know what you think!
Very cool.  I will dig into this tonight!  Thanks!
